+import { join } from 'node:path'
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
+
+import test from 'ava'

+import { createCanvas, getTextRenderer, GlobalFonts, Path2D, setTextRenderer } from '../index'

+GlobalFonts.registerFromPath(
+  join(fileURLToPath(new URL('.', import.meta.url)), 'fonts', 'Lato-Regular.ttf'),
+  'AntialiasLato',
+)
+
+function uniqueColors(data: Uint8ClampedArray): Set<number> {
+  const colors = new Set<number>()
+  for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i += 4) {
+    const rgba = ((data[i] << 24) | (data[i + 1] << 16) | (data[i + 2] << 8) | data[i + 3]) >>> 0
+    colors.add(rgba)
+  }
+  return colors
+}
+
+function uniqueAlphas(data: Uint8ClampedArray): Set<number> {
+  const alphas = new Set<number>()
+  for (let i = 3; i < data.length; i += 4) {
+    alphas.add(data[i])
+  }
+  return alphas
+}
+
+test('ctx.antialias getter/setter, defaults, invalid values, and WebIDL coercion', (t) => {
+  const canvas = createCanvas(16, 16)
+  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d')
+
+  t.is(ctx.antialias, 'default')
+
+  for (const mode of ['none', 'gray', 'subpixel', 'default'] as const) {
+    ctx.antialias = mode
+    t.is(ctx.antialias, mode)
+  }
+
+  ctx.antialias = 'none'
+  for (const invalid of ['invalid', 'NONE', 'Default', 'Gray', 'Subpixel', '', ' none', 1, null, undefined]) {
+    ;(ctx as any).antialias = invalid
+    t.is(ctx.antialias as string, 'none', `invalid value ${String(invalid)} should be ignored`)
+  }
+
+  // WebIDL DOMString conversion runs toString() on objects and rejects Symbol
+  ctx.antialias = 'default'
+  ;(ctx as any).antialias = { toString: () => 'none' }
+  t.is(ctx.antialias as string, 'none')
+
+  t.throws(
+    () => {
+      ;(ctx as any).antialias = Symbol('x')
+    },
+    { instanceOf: TypeError },
+  )
+  t.is(ctx.antialias as string, 'none')
+})

+# Threat model
+
+## What this is
+
+`bare-path` is compiled into Bare. It is listed in `src/builtins.json`, so every Bare process has it. That holds whether or not the process sealed, and no code has to load anything to reach it.
+
+So this addon is part of Bare, and [Bare's threat model](https://github.com/holepunchto/bare/blob/main/docs/threat-model.md) covers it. Read that one first. This one only says where this addon sits in it.
+
+## What it inherits
+
+- **The promise.** Bare promises a sealed process gets no new native code. This addon is native code that is already in, so the seal neither adds it nor takes it away.
+- **The attacker.** Untrusted JavaScript in a sealed process. It writes what it likes, runs on as many threads as it wants, and calls anything it can reach in any order and all at once. It can reach all of this addon.
+- **The trust.** This addon is trusted, because Bare compiles it in. Whatever you compile in is your security policy, and this is one of the things you picked.
+- **The walls.** The same table applies. A thread is not a wall and neither is a realm, so nothing here gets to assume it is alone.
+- **The rules.** What Bare says to report, and what Bare says is not a bug, is the same here.
+
+## What counts
+
+- **Counts:** `binding.c` and the JavaScript that ships with it. Sealed JavaScript reaches all of it without loading a thing.
+- **Does not count:** tests, benchmarks, and scratch code.
+
+## What this addon adds
+
+String manipulation, and `cwd`, which gives back the process working directory.
+
+`cwd` is the only thing here that reaches outside the process. What it gives away is one path, which tells sealed code a little about how the host filesystem is laid out.
+
+Nothing here touches the filesystem. Joining a path does not open it. Reaching a store still needs a protocol, and this addon has none to give.
+
+## Where the risk is
+
+The C handles paths that an attacker chose, and the Windows rules are the fiddly part.
+
+There is one more thing, and it is not about memory. What comes out of here feeds decisions made elsewhere. If something treats a path as safe because this normalized it, then this addon and the OS disagreeing matters at that call site. +
+- Memory bugs in `binding.c` that JavaScript can reach, above all the buffer sizing in `cwd` and the Windows path parsing
+- Any output that differs from what the platform itself resolves the same input to
+- Anything on Bare's report list
+

test: keep failed sequences and their nested groups literal (#169)

Bash keeps a group literal, along with every group nested in it, when its
body has a top-level `..` but is not a valid sequence. A `}` only closes a
group once a top-level `,` or `..` has come before it, so a `{` with no
comma can run past its matching `}` to a later one and become such a
failed sequence. main already follows both rules, but no test pinned
them, so #166 could change them without a test failing.

* feat: expose expand as a default export

* test: cover default export behavior

whitespace, equality boundaries, and malformed loose alternatives.

- Tests only; no production behavior changes.

## Stack
First of two stacked PRs; followed by #918. Contains only commit
1eda6b48b211d87b9f5857a6e53361abe7622ef8. Merge this PR before the
performance implementation.

fix: improve range parsing performance (#918)

## Summary
- Replace comparator whitespace normalization with a regex-free scanner
that preserves legacy match boundaries.
- Cache numeric lookahead to avoid repeatedly scanning overlapping digit
runs.
- Share the ECMAScript whitespace definition between production and
tests, using a byte lookup table rather than a Set.
- Add legacy compatibility checks and large-prefix/numeric-input
regression coverage.

## Stack
Originally stacked on #917, which was squash-merged into `main` as
7257c14239476205b4b0bf7e47b07b3e7a517be6. Rebased onto `main` after that
merge so this PR contains only the comparator normalization
implementation and its tests. The implementation patch is unchanged.

## Validation
- Full `npm test` passed: 54 test files, 100% coverage, ESLint, and
template checks.
- Differential review: 302,520 scanner cases and 100,000 Range cases
matched the parent implementation.
- Whitespace lookup: 196,608 differential cases matched the original
scanner across all UTF-16 code units.
- Large invalid-prefix parsing improved dramatically; numeric-lookahead
access counts scaled linearly through one million characters.

## Performance tradeoff
Local Node v26 benchmarks showed approximately 6–7% slower ordinary
uncached Range parsing versus the original regex. The shared byte-table
lookup did not introduce the additional slowdown observed with Set-based
membership checks. Measurements are local microbenchmarks, not
cross-runtime guarantees.
